Members and non-members alike are invited to pursue certification leading to designation as a Certified Professional in Healthcare Information and Management System (CPHIMS). A. What does CPHIMS certification involve? The CPHIMS certification program conducted by HIMSS and has three components: - Eligibility requirements - Baccalaureate degree plus five (5) years of associated information and management systems experience, three (3) of those years in healthcare OR - Postgraduate degree plus three (3) years of associated information and management systems experience, two (2) of those years in healthcare. - A 115 item multiple choice examination that tests competencies in health information management. - A renewal requirement every three (3) years (completed by demonstration of 45 contact hours of continuing professional education in information and management systems, with a minimum of 25 contact hours from HIMSS or HIMSS-approved continuing professional activities). Certification is valid for three years, after which point it must be renewed through retesting or documentation of continuing professional education. Start the process of becoming CPHIMS certified by downloading the Candidate Handbook and Application from the HIMSS web site (www.himss.org/getcertified). To schedule, reschedule and cancel exam: HIMSS® - Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society Demonstrate your expertise and experience as a health information and technology professional with certification from the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society® (HIMSS®). In a field experiencing vast change, it is important to possess a standard body of knowledge and an up-to-date skillset. HIMSS certifications show your stakeholders that you are well informed and well prepared for the next step in your career pathway. The Certified Associate in Healthcare Information and Management Systems® (CAHIMS®) certification is a pathway for expanding and diversifying industry knowledge for both early careerists and those with more experience. The Certified Professional in Healthcare Information and Management Systems® (CPHIMS®) is a certification program for experienced professionals, acknowledging and honoring their proven expertise and commitment to the field. The Certified Professional in Digital Health Transformation Strategy (CPDHTS®) is a certification program for experienced professionals who specialize in the digital health transformation strategy, including everything from change management to governance and results tracking. Find information on the certification programs on the HIMSS website, email certification@himss.org, or call +1-703-722-0580. The Candidate Handbook for each HIMSS certification program contains valuable information regarding the certification program’s scope, eligibility requirements, application process, applicable fees, exam content, exam preparatory resources, exam administration logistics, and recertification requirements. All candidates should carefully review the Candidate Handbook (for the specific certification program which the candidate is pursuing) during the application process and before taking the certification examination. There are now two ways to take an HIMSS certification exam via computer. Candidates have the option to take the exam: - In person at a brick-and-mortar Exam Center (with locally compliant social distancing and sanitizing protocols in place), using the Exam Center’s computer equipment and internet connection; or - At the candidate’s home or office (or any qualifying location of the candidate’s choice) through a remotely-proctored internet-based testing platform, using the candidate’s own computer, webcam, microphone, and internet connection. Your Candidate ID # and Client Authorization ID # (as they appear on your Authorization to Test (ATT) Notice) are required to schedule your exam. Before scheduling your exam appointment, you must apply for certification, be deemed Eligible, and receive an Authorization to Test (ATT) Notice (with your Candidate ID# and Client Authorization ID #) from the HIMSS Certification Department. Your first (given) name and last (family) name as listed on your ATT Notice must EXACTLY MATCH your first name and last name as those appear on a currently valid, government-issued photo identification bearing your signature, which you must present at the exam center (or during the remotely-proctored exam administration); if there are any discrepancies during check-in, the proctor will not allow you to take the exam, you will be considered a “no show,” and you will forfeit your exam fee (i.e., you would need to pay the exam retake fee to reschedule your test). If your name does NOT exactly match, please email the HIMSS Certification Department at certification@himss.org at least ten (10) days prior to your test date. If you require any special accommodations for testing, complete and submit the Request for Special Examination Accommodations form included in the Candidate Handbook and submit the completed form with all supporting documentation to certification@himss.org after submitting your certification application. To schedule your exam (either at a brick-and-mortar Exam Center or via live, remote proctoring), please Log in to your Pearson VUE web account. If you are a first-time exam taker with Pearson VUE, you will need to create an account. Locate an exam center prior to scheduling your exam appointment. To schedule your remotely-proctored, internet-based exam at your home, office, or other location of your choosing, using your own computer, webcam, microphone, and internet connection, first confirm your computer’s compatibility with the remote proctoring platform (“OnVUE”). You must supply the computer that you will use for the certification exam. The computer must have a webcam (internal or external), microphone (internal or external), speakers (internal or external), and a stable internet connection, and you must be able to install the Pearson VUE OnVUE app on your computer on the day of your exam appointment. Verify that your computer and internet network will allow testing through OnVUE. Please ensure that you have application installation (e.g., Admin) privileges on the computer you will be using for the certification exam. After you have 100% passed (all green check-marks) the system test, you can proceed to schedule your remotely-proctored, internet-based exam. If you are unable to 100% pass the system test and you had attempted to check your system through a VDI or VPN connection, please try directly from the computer rather than through the VDI or VPN; most candidates are unable to use the OnVUE™ platform through a VDI or VPN. Also, check to ensure that your microphone and webcam are enabled (and correctly connected, if external). If you are still unable to pass the 100% system test, or if you will not have the necessary permissions to install the OnVUE app on your exam date, please schedule your exam at a brick-and-mortar Exam Center, instead. After scheduling your exam, please review your appointment confirmation email and ensure that you have the correct exam, date, time, first name and last name matching your government ID, and (if testing at a brick-and-mortar Exam Center) testing location. Reschedule Policy You must contact Pearson VUE or access your online Pearson VUE account (by clicking “Sign in” in the sidebar of this webpage) to reschedule your exam at least 48 hours prior to your appointment. Exams cannot be rescheduled less than 48 hours prior to (that is, within 48 hours of) your appointment. Failure to reschedule in time—or failure to appear for—your appointment will result in the forfeiture of your exam fee. Rescheduled exam appointments must be within your eligibility period; if your eligibility period will expire before your exam is able to be rescheduled, you will need to pay the exam retake fee to schedule your exam for a new eligibility period. Cancellation Policy You must contact Pearson VUE or access your online Pearson VUE account to cancel your exam at least 48 hours prior to your appointment. Exams cannot be cancelled less than 48 hours prior to (that is, within 48 hours of) your appointment. Failure to cancel in time or failure to appear for your appointment will result in the forfeiture of your exam fee. If you have rescheduled or cancelled within 48 hours of your appointment (or did not show up for your exam appointment), you will need to submit another application and pay the exam retake fee to reschedule your exam. Candidates applying to retake the exam will receive an updated eligibility determination from the HIMSS Certification Department and (if deemed Eligible) a new ATT Notice with a new Client Authorization ID#. We ask that you arrive at the test center 30 minutes before your scheduled appointment time. This will give you adequate time to complete the necessary sign-in procedures. If you arrive more than 15 minutes late for your appointment, you may be refused admission, and the exam fees will be forfeited. You will be required to present one form of original (no photocopies), currently valid (unexpired), government-issued ID that includes your name, photograph, and signature. The first and last name that you used to register must match exactly the first and last name on the ID that is presented on test day; if there is a difference between your first and last name as they appear on your ATT Notice and as they appear on the ID that you will present on test day, please contact the HIMSS Certification Department immediately at certification@himss.org. All IDs required must be issued by the country in which you are testing; alternatively, if you do not have a qualifying ID issued from the country in which you are testing, an International Travel Passport from your country of citizenship is required. If possible, please bring a second government identification (that matches the same requirements as the primary ID) to your exam appointment, in case there is an issue with your primary identification. If you have any questions or concerns about the ID you are required to bring with you to the testing center for admittance to your exam, please contact Pearson VUE customer service. No personal items may be taken into the testing room. This includes but is not limited to all bags, books not authorized by the sponsor, notes, phones, pagers, watches, and wallets. No breaks, food, or beverages are allowed during the exam. All personal items other than the identification document must be locked in a locker (at an Exam Center) and outside of the testing area, for exam security purposes. No breaks are allowed during the exam, and no food or beverages may be consumed during the exam. Please be prepared to take the entire exam without breaks, eating, or drinking. If testing via OnVUE, please be advised that if you depart from the camera view / testing area at any time during the exam, your exam will be terminated immediately, and your score will be based on the exam items you have completed up to that point in time. In the healthcare IT field, certification has a significant impact on salary. But the sheer number of health information technology (health IT) credentials available to today’s professionals makes it difficult to narrow down the choices. How do you decide which credential best suits your professional goals and aspirations? Below, explore five respected and widely-known healthcare IT certifications: Epic, CPHIMS, CAHIMS, CHTS, and CHISP. Certified Associate of Health Information and Management Systems (CAHIMS) What is the CAHIMS credential? Awarded by the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS), this healthcare IT certification demonstrates professional knowledge of health IT and management systems. CAHIMS is usually earned by entry-level professionals with five or fewer years of experience in the field. Why is the CAHIMS beneficial? Though it’s designed for entry-level health IT professionals, systems analysts and health IT managers most often have the CAHIMS credential, according to HIMSS. It proves to current and future employers that an individual has professional health information technology knowledge and a commitment to career advancement. How can one earn CAHIMS certification? To be eligible to sit for the 115-question CAHIMS certification exam, you need only a high school diploma or equivalent. Epic Certification What is Epic certification? Epic Systems professional credentials can be earned by health IT specialists who implement and work on Epic electronic health record software used by hospitals and other healthcare organizations. Why is Epic certification beneficial? This healthcare IT certification demonstrates your proficiency in one or more Epic software modules: - ASAP: emergency room - Beacon: medical oncology - Cadence: scheduling and tracking patient appointments - Cupid: cardiology - EpiCare Ambulatory/Inpatient: clinical documentation, order entry, e-prescribing - Kaleidoscope: ophthalmology - OpTime/Anesthesia: scheduling and documentation for surgical procedures - Prelude/ADT: patient registration system - Radiant: radiology - Stork: obstetrics - Willow: pharmacy Epic certification is difficult to achieve but highly sought-after because Epic software is so popular. Epic consultants who travel to hospitals and assist with Epic Systems implementations are in high demand. These positions are lucrative—in 2013, the average Epic consultant made $139,000. How can one earn Epic certification? If you don’t work at Epic, you need to be sponsored by a healthcare employer to pursue Epic certification. Then, you must complete on-site training at Epic’s headquarters in Verona, Wisconsin and pass a proficiency exam. For more about Epic certification, see this UW graduate’s story. He earned the EpicCare Ambulatory credential and credited his Bachelor of Science in Health Information Management and Technology with preparing him for the certification process. Certified Professional in Health Information and Management Systems (CPHIMS) What is the CPHIMS credential? Also awarded by HIMSS, CPHIMS certification demonstrates an international standard of professional knowledge and competence in healthcare information and management systems. Why is the CPHIMS beneficial? While the CAHIMS certification is typically earned by entry-level professionals, the CPHIMS healthcare IT certification is earned by experienced professionals. According to HIMSS, more than half of those with a CPHIMS credential are in a leadership role: chief information officers, managers, directors, or vice presidents of an IT or IS department; with CEOs, CMIOs, CNOs, CMOs, nurses, registered pharmacists, and other senior staff roles, as well. Top work environments for CPHIMS include hospitals (45%), healthcare consulting firms (16%), academic medical centers (11%), federal, state, and local government offices (8%) and more. Having CPHIMS certification both increases credibility and demonstrates professional knowledge. How many people currently hold the CPHIMS credential? As of October 2018, 3,845 people hold the credential—85% in the United States and 15% in more than 30 different countries. Wisconsin has 87 professionals with the CPHIMS credential. How can one earn CPHIMS certification? You must pass the 115-question certification exam to become CPHIMS certified. To be eligible for the exam, you must meet one of these requirements: - A bachelor’s degree and five years of information and management systems experience, three of those years being in healthcare - A graduate degree and three years of information and management systems experience, two of those years being in healthcare Certified Healthcare Technology Specialist (CHTS) What is the CHTS credential? CHTS certification, awarded by the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA), denotes one’s ability to effectively implement and manage the use of electronic health records. This includes being able to assess workflows, select hardware and software, work with vendors, install and test systems, and diagnose IT problems. Why is the CHTS beneficial? For those seeking to manage and implement EHR systems, the CHTS credential demonstrates ability as well as commitment to the health IT industry. There are six separate CHTS exams, depending on which health IT workforce role you want to specialize in: - Clinician/practitioner consultant - Implementation manager - Implementation support specialist - Practice workflow and information management redesign - Technical/software support staff - Trainer How can one earn CHTS certification? You must pass the CHTS certification exam, administered by AHIMA. It’s recommended you have some experience or training in health IT before sitting for the exam, but there are no official requirements. Certified Health Informatics Systems Professional (CHISP) What is the CHISP credential? This credential is awarded by the American Society of Health Informatics Managers (ASHIM) and demonstrates mastery of general technical healthcare industry knowledge in computer science, healthcare regulations, billing, data security, healthcare operations, data-mining, medical terminology, and other health IT areas. Why is the CHISP beneficial? Healthcare professionals seeking IT mastery for career opportunities or IT professionals who want to get a foothold in the healthcare industry would benefit from becoming CHISP certified. How can one earn CHISP certification? You must pass the 150-question CHISP certification exam. To qualify to sit for the exam, applicants must either complete the ASHIM Health IT Professional training program or have three years of IT experience. ____ WHAT’S NEXT? Key Information: - The CAHIMS certification is ideal for entry-level professionals or career changers seeking foundational knowledge in healthcare IT. - The CPHIMS certification is designed for experienced HIT/HIM professionals aiming for leadership or strategic roles. - Both certifications validate expertise in healthcare information systems, with differing eligibility requirements and career outcomes. - Earning either credential can enhance job prospects, with CPHIMS holders typically earning higher salaries and managing more complex responsibilities. In the United States, healthcare information technology (HIT) is part of daily life. Over 58% of adults use the Internet to seek health information. Then, there’s the 41.5% of adults who use it to communicate with their doctors. Hospitals and doctors use telemedicine, e-prescribing systems, and electronic public health reporting. More than 1.3 billion people use telemedicine services today. The bottom line: Now is the best time to pursue the CAHIMS or CPHIMS credential. Doing so means tapping into a high demand for HIT professionals. In this article, we’ll discuss the various aspects of the CAHIMS vs CPHIMS debate. You’ll learn their prerequisites, key differences, and career outcomes, among others. This way, you can make an informed decision between the two credentials. The Healthcare Information & Management Systems Society (HIMSS) awards both credentials. Once you’re a member, you can network with over 100,000 individual members. Both the CAHIMS and CPHIMS credentials highlight expertise in HIT. However, these cater to different educational levels, work experience, and career goals. The CAHIMS certification is for entry-level and early-career HIT professionals. The CPHIMS certification is an advanced certification for experienced HIT professionals. Read on for more about the CAHIMS vs CPHIMS similarities and differences. Related: - Best Online Health Informatics Certifications - Best Telehealth and Telemedicine Certifications - Top Healthcare Certifications to Boost Your Job Prospects - Best Careers with a Health Information Technology Associates? - Top Health Information Technology Associate’s Degrees Overview of CAHIMS Certification Start your career as a Certified Associate in Healthcare Information and Management Systems (CAHIMS). Think of it as the best stepping stone toward leadership positions in the future. What Is CAHIMS? Again, the CAHIMS credentials are for entry-level or early-career HIT and HIMS professionals. Earning it validates your foundational knowledge and skills in HIT and HIMS. Who Should Pursue CAHIMS? The CAHIMS certification is ideal for: - Recent graduates starting their careers in HIT - Individuals new to the HIT field - Professionals who want to make a career change or transition into HIT Core Competencies Covered As an entry-level certification, it covers core competencies in: - Healthcare environment - IT and systems management - Organizational leadership Eligibility Requirements The CAHIMS credential is the most accessible certification with basic eligibility requirements, including: - A high school diploma or its equivalent is required. - A bachelor’s degree in a healthcare or technology-related field is recommended but isn’t required. Even current enrollment in an associate’s or bachelor’s degree program is acceptable. - No work experience is required. You must pass the CAHIMS certification exam to earn the credential. Overview of CPHIMS Certification The Certified Professional in Healthcare Information & Management Systems (CPHIMS) credential is the next step. What Is CPHIMS? The CPHIMS certification is an advanced certification for experienced HIT and HIMS professionals. Earning it validates your: - Technical expertise in HIT and HIMS - Project management skills in HIT and HIMS - Strategic leadership and operational insights in the healthcare sector - In-depth understanding of business process and clinical process integration Think of it as your competitive edge in career advancement opportunities. Who Should Pursue CPHIMS? The CPHIMS certification is ideal for: - Mid-career HIT/HIM professionals who want to formalize their knowledge and skills - Senior-level HIT/HIM professionals seeking to highlight their expertise in complex healthcare systems In their cases, their career goals include getting into leadership roles. Core Competencies Covered The CPHIMS certification covers more advanced topics in: - Healthcare and technology environment - Systems analysis, design, and selection - Human resources, management, and leadership CPHIMS-certified professionals can lead programs that combine business, IT, and clinical care. Eligibility Requirements There are two pathways toward earning the CPHIMS credential: Bachelor’s Degree Pathway - At least a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college - At least five years of relevant HIT or HIM experience, of which at least three years were in a healthcare setting Master’s Degree Pathway - At least a master’s degree from an accredited college - At least three years of relevant experience, of which at least two years were in a healthcare setting Passing the rigorous CPHIMS certification exam is the final hurdle. Key Differences Between CAHIMS and CPHIMS Here’s a simplified CAHIMS vs CPHIMS comparison table with these elements factored in: - Target Audience - Level of Expertise - Experience Required - Career Goals Alignment - Exam Difficulty and Scope - Cost Comparison - Period of Validity | CAHIMS | CPHIMS | | Entry-level and early-career HIT/HIM professionals, career changers | Advanced HIT/HIM professionals | | Foundational knowledge and skills | Advanced professional competencies | | Little to no experience is required. | Requires between three and five years of relevant experience. Depending on the pathway, 2-3 years relevant experience in healthcare settings. | | Getting started in healthcare IT roles | Transitioning into leadership, senior, or strategic roles | | Basic HIT theories, concepts, and principles | Advanced technical, managerial, and strategic competencies | | Lower exam fees | Higher exam fees and more intensive exam preparation | | Three years, renewable | Three years. Renewable | Exam Structure and Preparation for Both Certifications Both healthcare IT certifications have rigorous certification exams. You must prepare well and well in advance for either of these exams. While you’re allowed to retake an exam, you’ll spend more time, effort, and money. CAHIMS Certification Exam Overview The CAHIMS certification exam consists of 115 multiple-choice questions (100 scored and 15 unscored). Candidates have two hours to complete it. While it’s a relatively accessible exam, intensive preparation is still a must. Your study preparation must cover the following topics: - Basic healthcare IT concepts - Overview of healthcare systems and workflows - Introductory project management principles If you pass it, you’ll receive a certificate of recognition about eight weeks after the exam. CPHIMS Certification Exam Details The CPHIMS computer-based certification exam consists of 115 multiple-choice questions. Of these questions, 100 are scored questions, while 15 are unscored pretest questions. Candidates have two hours to complete it. Content areas covered include: - Healthcare and technology environment - Systems analysis, design, and selection If you pass it, you’ll immediately receive your results upon completion. Intensive exam prep is a must because of its rigorous nature. Study Resources for Each Go for the official sources for reliable and updated resources. - HIMSS certification guide - HIMSS study guides and practice exams - Online prep courses Attend HIMSS Learning Center webinars, too. Once you have earned the CAHIMS or CPHIMS credential, look for its CEU opportunities, too. Career Outcomes and Salary Expectations Deciding between CAHIMS or CPHIMS for career growth depends on many factors. You must consider your work experience and career goals, among others. CAHIMS Career Paths You’re qualified for these jobs with the CAHIMS credential. - Health IT analyst - Support specialist - Data entry and operations roles - Entry-level project assistant in IT departments CPHIMS Career Paths If you’re a CPHIMS-certified professional, you’re qualified for these jobs. - Health informatics manager - IT director - Consultant or systems implementation lead - Clinical applications manager Average Salaries CAHIMS-certified professionals earn between $55,000 and $75,000 in average annual salaries. CPHIMS-certified professionals earn higher salaries – between $85,000 and $120,000+ every year. Earning both certifications brings long-term career benefits. You’ll have improved career advancement prospects and higher earning potential. Gaining recognition as an authority in HIT/HIM is also a benefit. Keep in mind, however, that with certification comes increased responsibilities. You’ll lead and manage HIT teams and projects, for example. Which Certification Should You Choose? Choosing the best healthcare information systems certification is easier if you know its eligibility requirements. Then, you must consider your education, career goals, and work experience. Afterward, you can choose the certification that aligns with your circumstances. Choose CAHIMS If You: - Are new to healthcare IT and want a solid credential to back up your applications - Are a student or recent graduate who wants a competitive edge in the job market - Want to build foundational knowledge in HIT and HIM Choose CPHIMS If You: - Already work in healthcare or IT with at least three years of relevant experience - Are aiming for leadership or consulting roles in HIT/HIM - Want formal recognition of your advanced skills in organizational leadership, strategy, and systems analysis You must understand the differences between entry-level vs advanced healthcare IT certifications. This way, you can make an informed choice between them. Continuing Education and Certification Renewal Both CAHIMS and CPHIMS certifications require renewal every three years. Of course, you may or may not choose to renew it. But you’re well-advised to do so because it’s a valuable credential. The basic renewal requirements include: - Earn at least 45 Continuing Education Units (CEUs) over three years. - Pay renewal fees ($319 for members; $429 for non-members). - Stay active in professional development, such as conferences, webinars, and publications. HIMSS provides multiple opportunities to maintain certification. Conclusion In conclusion, the CAHIMS and CPHIMS credentials cater to different individuals based on their education and experience. The CAHIMS certification is an entry-level credential. The CPHIMS certification is an advanced professional credential. Choose between these two credentials based on your current career stage, goals, and experience. Start by earning the CAHIMS certification. When you gain relevant work experience, aim for the CPHIMS certification. Think of the CAHIMS-to-CPHIMS journey as part of your lifelong professional growth. Check out the official HIMSS website for more information. You’ll agree that both the CAHIMS and CPHIMS credentials offer the best value.

15 Aug Career Spotlight: Three of the Most Beneficial Healthcare IT Certifications The job market is booming for those in the field of healthcare IT. Job growth and high median salaries make these careers particularly desirable. In order to obtain one of the coveted healthcare IT positions, a candidate needs his or her resume to include the requisite training and/or experiences. In many cases, proper certification is required or highly preferred. Below are 3 of the healthcare IT certifications that are among the most beneficial in the industry. CPHIMS and CAHIMS Certification Two popular certifications, the Certified Associate in Health Information & Management Systems (CAHIMS) and Certified Professional in Health Information & Management Systems (CPHIMS), are offered through the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS) and are widely recognized in the healthcare IT field. The CAHIMS is typically obtained by a candidate who is looking to break into the industry. Only a high school diploma or the equivalent is required to earn the certificate. Certification is achieved via a 115 question and costs between $150 to $245 to sit for the exam at a virtual testing center. A host of review materials are available for the test through HIMSS. The CPHIMS certificate is a means for a healthcare IT professional to establish his or her expertise in the field. Payscale.com associates the certification with positions such as Chief Information Officer and Information Technology Director and a median salary of approximately $104,000. In order to qualify for the certification, HIMSS lists the following degree and career requirements: • Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university plus five (5) years of information and management systems experience*, three (3) of those years in a healthcare setting. or • Graduate degree or higher from an accredited college or university plus three (3) years of information and management systems experience*, two (2) of those years in a healthcare setting. Like the CAHIMS, the CPHIMS test has 115 questions, and it costs between $295 and $410 to take the exam at a virtual testing center. Review materials are available through HIMSS. CHTS Certification The American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) offers an industry-recognized certification option known as the Certified Healthcare Technology Specialist certificate (CHTS). The CHTS certificate is broken down into the following subcategories: · The Clinician/Practitioner Consultant Examination (CHTS-CP) · Implementation Manager Examination (CHTS-IM) · Implementation Support Specialist Examination (CHTS-IS) · Practice Workflow & Information Management Redesign Specialist (CHTS-PW) · Technical/Software Support Staff Examination (CHTS-TS) · Trainer Examination (CHTS-TR) Eligibility for CHTS certifications relies on job experience rather than education, and does not require any specific training or degree. All exams cost $299 to take at a virtual testing center, though free vouchers are available to those who demonstrate financial hardship. The 3 hour exams consist of 125 multiple choice questions. AHIMA states that the passage rates vary between 62-76%, depending on the subcategory. Review materials and courses are not available through AHIMA, but the organization offers “exam blueprints” in order for the candidate to create their own study guide. HCISPP Certification The final certification identified in this post is the HealthCare Information Security and Privacy Practitioner (HCISPP) certificate offered by Inspire a Safe and Secure Cyber World ((ISC)²). Geared for professionals with experience in privacy and security within the healthcare sector, (ISC)² lists the eligibility requirements as: - A minimum of two years of cumulative, paid work experience - In one or more knowledge areas of the HCISPP Common Body of Knowledge (CBK) that includes security, compliance and privacy Individuals without the career experience can also complete the exam to achieve an Associate of (ISC)2 designation. The HCISPP exam is a 3 hour, 125 question test completed at a Pearson Vue testing center. The cost of the exam varies as professional organizations can purchase vouchers to offer their employee candidates. (ISC)² offers a host of review courses available with a choice of in-class training and self-study. Frequently cited as a high value certificate by healthcare IT and other business publications, individuals with the HCISPP certificate have an average salary of approximately $127,000, according to Infosec Institute. Professional titles with this certification include Information Security Manager, Information Technology Manager, Compliance Officer and Risk Analyst. The Certified Professional in Healthcare Information and Management Systems (CPHIMS®) exam is designed to test an individual’s understanding of a well-defined body of knowledge in professional practice in healthcare information and management systems. Those who succeed have established themselves as CPHIMS for a period of five years. Click “Start Test” above to take a free CPHIMS practice exam, and check out our premium-quality CPHIMS test prep resources by clicking the links below! Exam Eligibility To be eligible for this exam, you must meet one of the following requirements: - You must hold a baccalaureate degree and have at least five years of information and management systems experience - You must hold a graduate degree or higher and have at least three years of information and management systems experience - You must have at least 10 years of information and management systems experience CPHIMS Exam Outline The CPHIMS certification exam contains 100 multiple-choice questions and has a time limit of 2 hours. The exam is split into four content areas, and the questions are designed to evaluate you on three cognitive areas: - Recall: Recall or recognize specific information - Application: Comprehend, relate, or apply knowledge to new or changing situations - Analysis: Analyze and synthesize information, determine solutions, or evaluate the usefulness of a solution I. Healthcare and Technology Environments (25%) The questions in this area assess your knowledge and skills pertaining to the following: - Articulating characteristics and services of different types of healthcare organizations - Describing the roles and responsibilities of healthcare information and management systems professionals within the organizational structures in which they work - Evaluating trends in healthcare technology and implementing strategies to improve patient outcomes - Articulating characteristics of interrelationships across and within healthcare organizations - Articulating characteristics of technology infrastructure that support the healthcare environment - Recognizing the impact of commonly accepted regulations, laws, accreditation, and other local and state rules that govern critical healthcare information and systems management services - Articulating characteristics of applications commonly used in healthcare II. Clinical Informatics (20%) The questions in this area assess your knowledge and skills pertaining to the following: - Basic clinical vocabulary and terms frequently represented in healthcare informatics - Developing and implementing system functionality to optimize clinical effectiveness and efficiencies - Basic clinical metrics frequently represented in informatics - Developing mechanisms to facilitate ongoing clinical content and decision-support tools - Interpreting operational and clinical outcomes through the use of various data analytics tools - Basic healthcare IT vocabulary and terms frequently represented in healthcare informatics III. Healthcare Information and Systems Management (30%) The questions in this area assess your knowledge and skills pertaining to the following: - Analysis - Design - Selection - Implementation - Support - Maintenance - Testing for evaluation - Privacy and security IV. Management and Leadership (25%) The questions in this area assess your knowledge and skills pertaining to the following: - Evaluating performance - Maintaining organizational competencies on current IT technologies and trends - Contributing to organizational strategic planning - Developing and implementing an IT strategic plan and departmental objectives that align and support organizational strategies and goals - Evaluating effectiveness and user satisfaction - Employing comparative analytics - Presenting interpretations and recommendations of data analyses to decision makers - Evaluating staff competency in information and management system skills - Defining roles, job descriptions, and responsibilities for healthcare IT functions - Managing budget and financial risks - Managing contractual agreements with partners and vendors Check out Mometrix's CPHIMS Study Guide Get practice questions, video tutorials, and detailed study lessons Get Your Study GuideRegistration To register for the CPHIMS exam, you must submit an application on the HIMSS website. Your application does not have to include proof of eligibility, but you must include the applicable application fee. | Member Status | Fee | |---|---| | HIMSS Individual Organizational Affiliate Member | $499 | | HIMSS Regular Member | $579 | | HIMSS Corporate Member | | | HIMSS Student Member | | | Non-member | $699 | Once your application and fee have been reviewed and approved, you will be sent an Authorization to Test (ATT) via email. Once you receive your ATT, you will have 90 days to schedule an exam appointment with Pearson VUE. Test Day In-person Testing On the day of your exam, you should arrive at the Pearson VUE testing center 15-30 minutes earlier than the scheduled exam time. This will give you enough time to complete the check-in process. When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in and present your photo ID to the proctor. You will be photographed and asked to sign a roster and other rule forms. Personal items such as your cell phone, wallet, keys, and accessories are not allowed in the testing room, so they should be left at home or placed in a secure locker outside the testing area. Just before the exam starts, you will be given a brief tutorial on the testing system and will be asked to sign an NDA. Remote Testing Before the day of the exam, you should ensure your equipment meets the minimum requirements. You must have a desktop or laptop with a webcam and microphone, and you should take your exam in a private workspace. The exam cannot be taken on mobile devices, smartphones, or tablets. The technical requirements are detailed on Pearson’s website. On the day of your exam, you will be asked to show the remote proctor your testing space and submit a valid form of photo ID. The proctor will walk you through the examination process after the check-in process is complete. How the Exam is Scored Your CPHIMS score is calculated using a scaled scoring system. This system takes your raw score, which is how many questions you answered correctly, and converts it to a numerical score on a scale from 200 to 800. The minimum passing score is 600. You should receive your score report within eight weeks after testing. Requirements - Hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university, along with: - Five years of information and management systems experience, with three years in a healthcare setting; OR - Hold a graduate degree or higher from an accredited college or university, along with: - Three years of information and management systems experience, with two years in a healthcare setting; OR - Have at least 10 years of information and management systems experience, with eight years in a healthcare setting. Target audiences - Health information manager - Medical coder - Healthcare data analyst - Medical coding compliance auditor - Clinical documentation specialist - Medical research analyst - Medical records Abstractor

I’m excited to share that I recently earned the Certified Professional in Healthcare Information and Management Systems (CPHIMS®) certification from HIMSS. As Director of Support and Tech Ops at ETHERFAX, this certification not only represents a significant milestone in my career but also strengthens ETHERFAX’s commitment to advancing healthcare technology and improving patient care through innovative solutions. The CPHIMS® certification is widely recognized as a benchmark for healthcare IT professionals who aim to demonstrate their expertise in healthcare information and management systems. It validates a comprehensive understanding of the healthcare environment, IT infrastructure, and management systems-all of which are crucial for driving meaningful change in the industry. The certification covers key areas such as healthcare regulations, information management, and the latest technological innovations, enabling certified professionals to more effectively solve the complex challenges that organizations face. My Journey to CPHIMS® Certification Achieving this certification was a rigorous process and required dedication to mastering a wide range of topics critical to healthcare IT. The CPHIMS® exam covers three major areas: healthcare and technology environments, systems management, and administration. Preparing for the exam meant diving deep into subjects that are essential for navigating the real-world challenges as a healthcare IT professional, including topics on the healthcare regulatory environment, quality and safety initiatives, data management, project management, and strategic planning. While the preparation was intense, it was also incredibly rewarding. The process allowed me to connect theoretical knowledge with practical applications, drawing from my experiences at ETHERFAX and in previous roles. I gained new insights around interoperability with electronic health records (EHR) and healthcare information technology (HIT), data security measures, and healthcare policy, all of which are increasingly important as the industry shifts toward value-based care models and data-driven decision-making. The Future of Healthcare Information Management At ETHERFAX, our mission is to enable healthcare organizations to securely exchange critical patient information and other high-resolution documents. As the industry continues to evolve, healthcare facilities are increasingly looking for technology partners that can help them meet regulatory requirements, optimize workflows, and enhance patient outcomes. Achieving the CPHIMS® certification strengthens my ability to support these initiatives by providing a deeper understanding of the unique demands of healthcare IT and the strategic approaches needed to solve pressing challenges. The CPHIMS® certification also serves as a reminder of the responsibility we have as healthcare IT professionals to continually learn, adapt, and innovate. The healthcare industry is constantly evolving, and staying current with the latest advancements and best practices is essential to providing the best possible support to our customers. Thank you to everyone who has supported me on this journey. Here’s to the future of healthcare technology and the innovations that lie ahead! Together, we will continue making strides toward more efficient, higher-value care for patients.

Ever wondered how the right credentials can set you apart in the competitive field of healthcare information and management systems? The CPHIMS certification is your golden ticket, signaling to employers your mastery of technology and healthcare processes. In this article, we break down the CPHIMS certification requirements, outlining the crucial steps needed on your journey to recognition in the ever-evolving landscape of healthcare IT. With clarity and precision, we navigate the prerequisites, the exam preparation, and the certification maintenance – all tailored to boost your professional credentials. - 1. Meet the Educational Prerequisites - 2. Garner Relevant Work Experience - 3. Understand the Application Process - 4. Prepare for the CPHIMS Examination - 5. Schedule Your Examination - 6. Comply with Examination Policies - 7. Maintain Your Certification - Beyond CPHIMS – Additional Certifications - Career Prospects with CPHIMS - Conclusion: Your Path to CPHIMS Certification 1. Meet the Educational Prerequisites When embarking on the journey to obtaining a CPHIMS certification, meeting the educational prerequisites is your launching pad. This initial requirement is crucial in showcasing your commitment and readiness for the challenges ahead in healthcare information and management systems. Let’s walk through what you need: - Bachelor’s Degree: If your academic history includes a baccalaureate degree, you’re expected to complement it with five years of information and management systems experience. Not just any experience—it should be woven with threads from healthcare to meet the cphims certification requirements. - Graduate Degree: For the advanced degree holders, the road is a bit shorter. You can qualify with three years of relevant experience—yet again, healthcare must be the backdrop of your professional story. - Seasoned Professionals: If your journey so far hasn’t included a cap and gown ceremony, fret not. Ten years of professional experience in related fields can also pave the way to qualification. The catch here is ensuring that experience aligns with the cross-section of information systems and healthcare. To delve deeper into the academic and professional thresholds, consider perusing the CPHIMS Candidate Handbook, which encapsulates the essence of educational requirements eloquently. 2. Garner Relevant Work Experience The canvas of relevant work experience for CPHIMS is vast. It’s not just about the time spent behind a desk but the quality and relevance of your professional engagements. Take a look at what counts: - Systems Analysis and Design: Being the architect of information systems that stand strong against the winds of healthcare’s demands is a golden tick. - Implementation Experience: If you’ve been at the helm, steering complex information systems from blueprint to reality in a healthcare setting, you’ve hit the jackpot. - Management Engineering: Directing the orchestra of healthcare information management that turns data into symphonies of efficiency? Bravo—that’s what they’re looking for. For bachelors and masters, the magic numbers are three and two, respectively—the minimum years of healthcare experience you should bring to the table. A closer inspection of these CPHIMS eligibility requirements will ensure you’re on the right track. 3. Understand the Application Process Ready to turn your qualifications into action? Understanding the CPHIMS application process is your next milestone. Here’s a step-by-step guide to keep you on course: - Eligibility Review: Before anything else, have your eligibility vetted through HIMSS’s discerning lens. Ensure all your ducks—a.k.a. documents—are in a row. - Application Submission: Tailor your application to perfection and submit it via the HIMSS website. Crosscheck every detail to echo the sincerity of your pursuit. - Approval Await: A patient pause follows—await the HIMSS nod that propels you closer to the coveted certification. Beyond the basics, wrapping your head around deadlines and documentation nuances is vital. Wade through these intricacies with the guidance of HIMSS application insights. 4. Prepare for the CPHIMS Examination Preparation for the CPHIMS examination is both an art and a science. As you gear up to showcase your proficiency, let’s map out your strategy: - Solidify Your Study Plan: Sketch a blueprint of your study journey—decide when, where, and how you’ll conquer the syllabus. - Leverage Official Resources: The CPHIMS Review Course is your friend—befriend it. The self-assessment exam? That’s your trusty mirror, reflecting areas to polish. - Understanding the Examination Scope: Grasping the breadth and depth of the exam will add precision to your aim—dive into the CPHIMS Review Guide for clarity. The mantra is simple—plan, prepare, and practice. Donald Cox’s narrative of his experience in preparing for the CPHIMS exam illustrates the diligence required in this phase. 5. Schedule Your Examination With preparation underway, it’s time to carve your name onto an exam date. Scheduling your CPHIMS examination calls for attention to detail. Here are the steps to etch your exam into reality: - Receive Eligibility ID: Post-approval, an eligibility ID will reach you, serving as your golden ticket to exam booking. - Choose Your Venue: Worldly or remote? Testing centers span the globe, offering flexibility, while select HIMSS events bring the exam to you. - Set the Date: Align with the testing centers’ calendars and pick a date that allows ample time for preparation buffer. Booking details and considerations are neatly outlined for your convenience on the Pearson VUE website, where your path to certification seamlessly continues. 6. Comply with Examination Policies When the day of your CPHIMS examination arrives, adhering to the examination policies is as crucial as the knowledge you carry. The CPHIMS certification requirements are stringent, not to intimidate, but to maintain the integrity and professionalism of the process. Here’s how to ensure your exam day unfolds without a hitch: - Identification Protocol: Your ID is your passport to the exam. Ensure it matches the personal details you’ve provided during registration. - On-Site Exam Regulations: Be prepared for a rigorous testing atmosphere. Once the exam commences, there’s no stepping away until it’s complete. No snacks or sips are allowed—fuel up beforehand. - Remote Examination Conduct: For those opting for remote proctoring, the testing environment should be a bastion of calm, free from distractions and interruptions. The stringent policies safeguard the legitimacy and respect accorded to the CPHIMS credential. For a comprehensive understanding of what to expect, and to curate a checklist for your exam day, visit the official Pearson VUE guidelines. 7. Maintain Your Certification After the accolade of becoming CPHIMS-certified is proudly in your name tag, it’s about sustaining that status. Certification maintenance is an ongoing commitment—a promise to stay abreast with the pulsating rhythm of healthcare IT. Consider these mandates to continue exemplifying excellence: - Clock the Continuing Education Credits: Every three years, the quest for knowledge must be evidenced through 45 Continuing Education (CE) credits—of which, at least 25 should spring from HIMSS events or approved endeavors. - Opt for the Examination, Again?: You may choose to demonstrate your undiminished acumen by sitting for the CPHIMS examination anew, bypassing the CE route. Guard your certification like a cherished credential. Regularly refresh on the CPHIMS recertification rules to preclude any chance of lapsing. Beyond CPHIMS – Additional Certifications While the CPHIMS stands tall as a testament to your expertise in healthcare IT, complementing it with additional certifications can add more storylines to your professional narrative. Here are some noteworthy ones to consider: - CPHQ: This showcases your know-how in healthcare quality management, a perfect symbiosis with CPHIMS. - CMM: Consider this if you want to master medical management and stride into leadership roles confidently. - CPHRM: For those who have an eagle’s eye for recognizing risks and ensuring patient safety, this is your call. Fusing CPHIMS with these certifications can amplify your versatility and desirability in the industry. Peek into the gallery of additional certifications to select your next credential conquest. Career Prospects with CPHIMS Now, picture your future with a CPHIMS certification in hand. It’s not just a few letters after your name—it’s a beacon signaling your expertise in the intertwining worlds of healthcare and IT. With this designation, doors swing open: - Recognized Professionalism: You’re not just part of the crowd; you’re the crowd’s standout—a beacon of specialized knowledge. - Career Advancement: This certification can act as the jet fuel for your professional ascent, propelling you toward senior roles and specialized opportunities. - Global Recognition: Because the CPHIMS is a recognized standard, you gain an international passport to career prospects beyond borders. Wrap your imagination around the possibilities by exploring more on how CPHIMS certification shapes careers, and start your journey towards making a global impact. Conclusion: Your Path to CPHIMS Certification Recall the old adage, “A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step”? Your path to obtaining CPHIMS certification embodies that spirit. A meticulous confluence of education, experience, and endurance, this journey will appraise and elevate your professional capabilities significantly. Remember, walking through the demands of CPHIMS certification requirements isn’t just about personal accolades, it’s an investment in your future—a future enriched with know-how, recognition, and promising career prospects. As you move forward, keep the beacon of CPHIMS in sight, let it be your guide through the intricate world of healthcare information and management systems. With each stride, earn that reputation, the prestige, the honor it bestows. And when you’ve reached the summit, gaze back at the trail you’ve blazed—knowing it was well worth the climb. CPHIMS certification requirements guide professionals in healthcare information and management systems towards credential achievement and career advancement.

Designed to be a pathway for healthcare information and management systems careers, the Certified Associate in Healthcare Information and Management Systems (CAHIMS®) certification helps emerging professionals, who may or may not have experience, break into the field. The Certified Professional in Healthcare Information and Management Systems (CPHIMS®) is an internationally recognized professional certification program for experienced healthcare information and management systems professionals. The CPHIMS designation acknowledges and honors proven expertise and commitment. The Certified Professional in Digital Health Transformation Strategy (CPDHTS®) is an international certification program for advanced professionals to demonstrate professional knowledge and competence in digital health transformation strategy and digital health.
